title: [4/11/2021] Age when first giving birth
prompt: The chart below gives information about the age of women in Australia when they gave birth to their first child in 1966, 1986, and 2006. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The given bar chart compares the ages at which Australian women gave birth in 1966, 1986, and 2006.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the data suggest that women in Australia are progressively having children later over time. In addition, half of all first-time mothers in 2006 were between 30 and 34.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the figures for Australian women under 30, in 1966, a large majority of women started their family in their early 20s, at 68%, while the figures for those under 19 or in their late 20s made up similar proportions of about 40%. By 2006, falls of 28% and 37% were recorded in the figures for women under 19 and from 20 to 24, respectively. In contrast, the proportion of Australian women who had their firstborn in their late 20s only slightly increased to 41% over the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to the over-30 age brackets, the figures for females in their early and late 30s were relatively similar in 1966, at around 10%. From 1986 onwards, the former figure surged to 50%, becoming the most common age group to start a family, while the latter rose a slower pace, ending up at just over 30% at the end of the period. Finally, the figures for women in their 40s and onwards showed little variation during the cited period, remaining at a fairly negligible proportion of under 5%.
